best_for: Readers with a large e-book collection across Kindle, Kobo and other devices who want one library to sort, convert and send books, for free.
description:
calibre is an e-book manager written and kept up by Kovid Goyal, who asks users for donations to keep development going. It aims to handle nearly everything you do with e-books in one program.

You can fill in or fix each book's title, author, ISBN, tags, cover and summary, and add your own fields to track what you have read and liked. calibre converts between dozens of formats and can build a table of contents along the way. Its own viewer has highlights, bookmarks and read aloud. It can also fetch news from sources such as The Guardian, BBC News and The Economist as an e-book, and its Content server lets you read your books on any device.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: calibre is GPL 3.0 software made by Kovid Goyal. There is no paid edition.

points.title: Windows 10 1809 or newer
points.text: The current release needs Windows 10 version 1809 or later and comes as a 64-bit installer for all users. Older Windows 10 builds need calibre 7.26, Windows 8 needs 5.44, and Windows 7 or Vista need 3.48.

points.title: Recent macOS only
points.text: calibre 9.19 needs macOS 14 Sonoma or later. On macOS 13 the last version is 7.26; Big Sur and Monterey stop at 6.29.

points.title: Linux: the author prefers his installer
points.text: The download page asks users not to use distribution packages, calling them often outdated, and offers a one-line installer that bundles its own libraries and needs glibc 2.34 or newer. The Flatpak listed here is not marked verified on Flathub and trails at 9.18.0.

points.title: Rolling back
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 112 versions, which helps if a new release breaks a plugin. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so older builds there come from calibre's own archive.
